entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3763"/><div sID="gen5397" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3763"/><hi type="bold">8. all the Philistines went up to seek David--</hi>in the hope of accomplishing his ruin (for so the phrase is used, <reference osisRef="1Sam.23.15">1Sa 23:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Sam.24.2">24:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Sam.24.3">3</reference>) before his throne was consolidated. Their hostility arose, both from a belief that his patriotism would lead him, ere long, to wipe out the national dishonor at Gilboa, and by fear, that in any invasion of their country, his thorough knowledge of their weak points would give him superior advantages. They resolved, therefore, to surprise and crush him before he was fairly seated on his throne. <div eID="gen5397" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3768"/><div sID="gen5403" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3768"/><hi type="bold">15. for God is gone forth before thee--</hi>"a sound of going in the tops of the mulberry trees," that is, the rustling of the leaves by a strong breeze suddenly rising, was the sign by which David was divinely apprised of the precise moment for the attack. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3769"/><div sID="gen5404" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3769"/><hi type="bold">16. from Gibeon ... to Gazer--</hi>Geba or Gibea (<reference osisRef="2Sam.5.25">2Sa 5:25</reference>), now Yefa, in the province of Judah. The line from this to Gazer was intersected by the roads which led from Judah to the cities of the Philistines. To recover possession of it, therefore, as was effected by this decisive battle, was equivalent to setting free the whole mountain region of Judah as far as their most westerly slope [Bertheau]. <chapter eID="1Chr.14"/>
